title: Lighthouse Beacon Controller
spec: Simulate a diagnostic node for an automated coastal lighthouse. The node requires no initial arguments and uses a test method taking no arguments to generate current conditions. You must provide distinct methods taking no arguments to read the main lamp intensity, read the rotation motor speed, read the backup battery charge, read the solar panel output, read the foghorn air pressure, read the external wind speed, read the internal tower temperature, and read the daylight sensor status. Include an entry function `lighthouse` that initializes the node, runs the test, and returns a tuple of the eight metrics. Example output: (10000.0, 5.5, 98.0, 250.0, 120.0, 45.0, 18.5, False).

title: Dialysis Machine Monitor
spec: Write a physiological monitor for a medical dialysis machine. The monitor takes no arguments to set up and includes a pulse method taking no arguments to update the fluid dynamics. Implement separate methods taking no arguments to fetch the blood flow rate, fetch the dialysate flow rate, fetch the venous pressure, fetch the arterial pressure, fetch the fluid removal goal, fetch the current fluid removed, fetch the dialysate temperature, and fetch the air bubble detection flag. Write an entry function `dialysis` that creates the monitor, triggers a pulse, and yields a list of the eight values. Example output: [300.0, 500.0, 150.0, -100.0, 2000.0, 800.0, 37.0, False].

title: Combine Harvester Dashboard
spec: Design a dashboard data source for an agricultural combine harvester. The data source is initialized without arguments and has a sample method taking no arguments to lock in the field data. Provide individual methods that take no arguments to return the crop throughput rate, return the grain tank fill percentage, return the threshing drum speed, return the concave clearance, return the sieve loss rate, return the stalk chopper engagement, return the header cutting height, and return the total harvested area. Create an entry function `harvester` that prepares the data source, takes a sample, and returns a tuple of the eight dashboard values. Example output: (45.5, 80.0, 900.0, 15.0, 1.5, True, 10.5, 125.0).

title: Mining Conveyor Belt System
spec: Model the system diagnostics of a subterranean mining conveyor belt. The diagnostics object is created with no arguments and uses a survey method taking no arguments to update internal logs. Implement separate parameterless methods to get the belt speed, get the ore payload weight, get the roller bearing temperature, get the drive motor current, get the belt tension force, get the dust suppression water flow, get the structural vibration level, and get the emergency pull cord status. Include an entry function `conveyor` that creates the diagnostics object, runs a survey, and outputs a list of the eight logged values. Example output: [2.5, 4500.0, 65.0, 120.0, 3000.0, 15.0, 0.8, False].

title: Nuclear Reactor Core Monitor
spec: Simulate the control center of a nuclear fission reactor. The control center requires no arguments for creation and features a synchronization method taking no arguments to read plant sensors. Provide distinct methods taking no arguments to retrieve the control rod insertion percentage, retrieve the primary coolant flow, retrieve the secondary coolant flow, retrieve the core temperature, retrieve the containment vessel pressure, retrieve the radiation containment level, retrieve the steam turbine speed, and retrieve the scram system readiness. Write an entry function `reactor` that initializes the center, synchronizes the sensors, and returns a tuple of the eight plant readings. Example output: (85.0, 10000.0, 8000.0, 315.0, 1.2, 0.05, 3600.0, True).

title: Commercial Escalator Sensor
spec: Build a status tracker for a heavy duty commercial escalator. The tracker requires no arguments to construct and includes a poll method taking no arguments to update mechanical metrics. You must write individual methods taking no arguments to report the step band speed, report the handrail tension, report the drive motor temperature, report the passenger load weight, report the vibration frequency, report the comb plate alignment, report the lubrication oil level, and report the emergency stop button status. Include an entry function `escalator` that sets up the tracker, polls the metrics, and yields a list of the eight mechanical parameters. Example output: [0.5, 120.0, 45.5, 850.0, 15.0, 0.1, 85.0, False].

title: Glass Blowing Kiln Controller
spec: Create a telemetry module for an industrial glass annealing kiln. The module takes no arguments to set up and uses a measurement method taking no arguments to capture internal conditions. Implement separate parameterless methods to check the main heating chamber temperature, check the cooling zone temperature, check the belt conveyor speed, check the gas pressure, check the oxygen mixture ratio, check the thermal stress level, check the exhaust draft rate, and check the door seal integrity. Write an entry function `kiln` that creates the module, captures a measurement, and returns a tuple of the eight conditions. Example output: (1200.0, 400.0, 1.5, 2.5, 20.0, 5.0, 150.0, True).

title: Hydroelectric Dam Control
spec: Model the sensory input of a hydroelectric dam control system. The model is instantiated without arguments and features an observation method taking no arguments to record the current state. Provide distinct methods taking no arguments to obtain the reservoir water elevation, obtain the penstock water pressure, obtain the wicket gate opening percentage, obtain the turbine rotational speed, obtain the generator output power, obtain the spillway flow rate, obtain the downstream river level, and obtain the fish ladder activity count. Include an entry function `dam` that instances the model, makes an observation, and outputs a list of the eight sensory inputs. Example output: [1200.5, 850.0, 75.0, 200.0, 500.0, 100.0, 45.0, 12].

title: Seaplane Water Landing Distance
spec: A seaplane needs to determine its landing distance on water. The logic inside `calculate(weight, conditions)` must first determine the approach speed based on the aircraft weight and the headwind velocity. Next, it must calculate the hydrodynamic drag during touchdown using the approach speed, wave height, and hull type index. Finally, it aggregates these to find the total stopping distance, returning a negative value if it exceeds the available lake length. Example input: weight five thousand, conditions containing wind ten, wave two, hull one point five, lake two thousand, resulting in output one thousand two hundred.

title: Pharmacokinetics Drug Clearance
spec: A hospital pharmacy calculates how long a drug remains in a patient. The logic inside `clearance(dosage, patient)` must first compute the volume of distribution using the patient body mass and the drug tissue binding factor. Next, it must determine the elimination rate constant from the liver function score and kidney filtration rate. Finally, it combines the distribution volume and elimination rate to find the half life, and then determines the total hours until the concentration falls below a target threshold. Example input: dosage five hundred, target ten, patient mass seventy, tissue factor zero point six, liver one, kidney ninety, resulting in output fourteen point five.

title: Subsea Telecom Cable Routing
spec: An engineering firm plans the deployment of a submarine communications cable. The logic inside `route(distance, seabed)` must calculate the required cable length by applying a slack factor to the distance based on the seabed depth profile and ocean current speed. Next, it must determine the number of optical repeaters needed by dividing the true cable length by the signal attenuation limit. Finally, it calculates the total deployment time considering the ship laying speed, which decreases linearly for every repeater spliced. Example input: distance eight thousand, depth three thousand, current two, attenuation hundred, resulting in output a tuple of length eight thousand four hundred, repeaters eighty four, days twenty.

title: Ballet Choreography Validator
spec: A dance academy checks if a proposed ballet routine is physically possible. The logic inside `validate(sequence, dancers)` must first calculate the fatigue score of the sequence by summing the difficulty tiers of all jumps and turns. Then, it evaluates the stage spacing by checking if the maximum cluster of dancers exceeds the safe area per person. Finally, it determines the routine viability by ensuring the fatigue score is below the stamina limit of the cast and the spacing is safe. Example input: sequence containing three jumps of tier two and one turn of tier three, five dancers, stamina fifteen, stage area fifty, resulting in output true.

title: Orchestral Stage Seating
spec: A conductor needs to map out orchestra seating for optimal acoustics. The logic inside `arrange(musicians, stage)` must first group the musicians into strings, woodwinds, brass, and percussion, counting the members in each. Next, it must calculate the depth required for each section using the stage width, the spacing needed per instrument type, and the acoustic projection angle. Finally, it checks if the total required depth fits within the available stage depth, returning a list of row coordinates for each section or an empty list if it fails. Example input: fifty strings, ten woodwinds, twelve brass, five percussion, stage width twenty, depth fifteen, resulting in output a list of four starting coordinates.

title: Maglev Levitation Gap
spec: A magnetic levitation train system adjusts its electromagnets to maintain a safe gap. The logic inside `levitate(train, track)` first computes the downward force using the train passenger mass and base vehicle mass. Then, it calculates the required magnetic coil current based on the downward force, the track magnetic permeability, and the target levitation gap. Finally, it checks the current against the cooling system capacity and returns the optimized current value, or zero if it exceeds safety limits. Example input: passenger mass five thousand, vehicle mass twenty thousand, permeability zero point eight, gap fifteen, cooling limit three hundred, resulting in output two hundred fifty.

title: Geodesic Dome Struts
spec: An architect is designing a geodesic dome and needs the exact measurements. The logic inside `geometry(radius, frequency)` must first determine the number of vertices and faces based on the subdivision frequency. Next, it calculates the lengths of the two distinct strut types, known as short and long, using the dome radius and the frequency dependent chord factors. Finally, it computes the total length of steel tubing required by multiplying the strut lengths by their respective quantities. Example input: radius ten, frequency two, resulting in output a tuple containing thirty short struts, thirty five long struts, and total length four hundred.

title: Pinball Flipper Physics
spec: A digital pinball game engine calculates the trajectory of a ball after it hits a flipper. The logic inside `strike(ball, flipper)` first calculates the impact momentum from the ball mass, its incoming velocity, and the flipper swing speed. Next, it determines the rebound angle using the flipper resting angle, the strike position along the flipper, and the rubber elasticity coefficient. Finally, it computes the new exit velocity components and returns them. Example input: ball mass eighty, velocity ten, flipper speed twenty, angle thirty, strike position zero point five, elasticity zero point seven, resulting in output a tuple of exit horizontal and vertical velocities.

title: Paintball Field Cover
spec: A tactical simulation evaluates a player position on a paintball field to determine their exposure. The logic inside `evaluate(obstacles, player)` must first calculate the line of sight blockage for each obstacle using its height, width, and distance from the player. Next, it evaluates the flanking vulnerability by checking the angular gaps between the effective obstacles against the known opponent positions. Finally, it computes a survival probability score based on the total blocked angles and the player stance height. Example input: three obstacles with dimensions, player stance crouching, two opponent angles, resulting in output seventy five point five.

title: Bonsai Branch Pruning
spec: A botanical garden automates care instructions for bonsai trees. The logic inside `prune(tree, season)` must first calculate the ideal branch length based on the tree trunk thickness, species growth rate, and the current season factor. Next, it evaluates each existing branch to determine if its internode distance and foliage density require trimming. Finally, it returns a list of specific cutting points for branches that exceed the ideal length or have insufficient foliage. Example input: trunk thickness five, species rate one point two, season spring, three branches with lengths ten and nodes two, resulting in output a list of two cutting points.

title: Maple Syrup Boiling
spec: A sugar shack needs to optimize the boiling process to turn maple sap into syrup. The logic inside `boil(sap, evaporator)` first calculates the water removal requirement by comparing the initial sap sugar percentage to the target syrup density. Next, it determines the boiling time based on the evaporator pan surface area, the wood fire heat output, and the ambient air temperature. Finally, it computes the hourly draw off rate of finished syrup and the total firewood cords required. Example input: sap volume one thousand, sugar two percent, area twenty, heat fifty, temp zero, resulting in output a tuple of boiling time twelve and draw off rate one point five.

title: Wind Turbine Pitch
spec: A wind farm controller adjusts turbine blade angles to maximize power without causing damage. The logic inside `pitch(wind, turbine)` must first determine the available wind kinetic energy using the wind speed, air density, and rotor swept area. Next, it calculates the ideal angle of attack to maintain the target rotation speed while preventing aerodynamic stall. Finally, if the wind speed exceeds the safety threshold, it overrides the angle to feather the blades completely, returning the final commanded angle in degrees. Example input: wind speed fifteen, density one point two, area five thousand, target speed twenty, resulting in output twelve point five.

title: Sailplane Thermal Soaring
spec: A flight computer for an unpowered glider calculates the optimal circling strategy inside a rising column of air. The logic inside `soar(glider, thermal)` first computes the aircraft sink rate at various bank angles using the wingspan, gross weight, and drag polar coefficients. Next, it evaluates the net climb rate by subtracting the sink rate from the thermal updraft strength at the corresponding turn radius. Finally, it identifies and returns the bank angle that yields the highest net climb rate. Example input: wingspan eighteen, weight four hundred, drag zero point zero two, thermal strength three, thermal radius fifty, resulting in output forty five.

title: Coral Reef Outplanting
spec: A marine biology team plans the restoration of a damaged reef by transplanting nursery corals. The logic inside `outplant(site, corals)` must first calculate the optimal grid spacing based on the coral species adult size, the historical growth rate, and the local water flow velocity. Next, it determines the total number of fragments that can fit in the designated site area while avoiding shaded zones cast by existing rocks. Finally, it returns the spacing distance and the maximum fragment capacity. Example input: site area five hundred, rock area fifty, adult size zero point five, growth rate zero point one, flow moderate, resulting in output spacing zero point eight, capacity six hundred.

title: Neon Sign Tube Bending
spec: A custom neon sign shop calculates the material needed to bend glass tubes into letters. The logic inside `fabricate(design, glass)` first computes the true arc length of each curved section using the bend radius and angle, adding it to the straight segments. Next, it determines the required heating time per bend based on the glass tube diameter, wall thickness, and color coating type. Finally, it returns the total raw glass length to cut and the estimated fabrication time in minutes. Example input: three bends of radius two and angle ninety, two straights of ten, diameter fifteen, thickness one, resulting in output total length twenty nine point four, time twelve.

title: Leather Tanning Drum
spec: A tannery optimizes the chemical bath for processing raw animal hides into leather. The logic inside `tan(hides, chemicals)` first calculates the total dry weight of the batch and the required volume of water to achieve the correct float ratio. Next, it determines the dosage of the tanning agent and buffering salts based on the hide thickness, desired softness, and target acidity level. Finally, it computes the drum rotation time and speed needed for full penetration, returning the water volume, agent weight, and time. Example input: fifty hides of thickness three, softness high, acidity four, resulting in output a tuple of water five hundred, agent twenty, time eight.

title: Meteorite Crater Dimension
spec: A planetary geology simulator estimates the size of a crater formed by a meteorite strike. The logic inside `impact(meteorite, surface)` first calculates the kinetic energy of the impactor using its mass and entry velocity. Next, it computes the transient crater volume by factoring in the impact angle, the target rock density, and the surface gravity of the planet. Finally, it derives the final crater diameter and depth by applying collapse and settling adjustments to the transient volume. Example input: mass ten thousand, velocity twenty thousand, angle forty five, density three, gravity nine point eight, resulting in output diameter fifty, depth ten.

title: Ham Radio Antenna
spec: An amateur radio operator calculates the physical dimensions for a dipole antenna. The logic inside `tune(frequency, cable)` first computes the theoretical half wavelength in free space based on the target transmission frequency. Next, it applies a velocity factor adjustment to determine the actual wire length, accounting for the insulation material and wire gauge. Finally, it calculates the impedance mismatch at the feed point to determine if an impedance matching transformer is required, returning the final wire lengths and a boolean flag. Example input: frequency fourteen point two, insulation factor zero point nine five, gauge twelve, resulting in output wire length nine point five, matching required true.

title: Drum Kit Tuning Tension
spec: A percussion technician calculates the optimal lug torque for tuning a drum set. The logic inside `tension(drum, head)` first determines the fundamental resonant frequency desired based on the drum shell diameter, depth, and wood material density. Next, it calculates the required uniform tension across the drum head using the fundamental frequency and the synthetic film thickness. Finally, it divides the total tension by the number of tuning lugs to output the specific torque needed per lug. Example input: diameter fourteen, depth six, wood density six hundred, frequency two hundred, thickness zero point two, lugs ten, resulting in output torque four point five.

title: Rock Climbing Cam Placement
spec: A climbing safety analyzer evaluates if a spring loaded camming device will hold a fall. The logic inside `place(crack, cam)` first calculates the expansion range percentage by comparing the rock crack width to the minimum and maximum dimensions of the cam. Next, it determines the holding power based on the expansion percentage, the rock surface friction coefficient, and the placement angle relative to the downward pull direction. Finally, it returns the maximum dynamic load the placement can sustain before slipping out. Example input: crack width thirty, cam min twenty, cam max forty, friction zero point six, angle ten, resulting in output maximum load twelve.

title: Hydrofoil Lift
spec: A naval architect calculates the speed at which a hydrofoil boat will rise above the water. The logic inside `lift(vessel, foil)` first computes the dynamic pressure acting on the underwater wings using the fluid density and the vessel velocity. Next, it determines the lift force generated by multiplying the dynamic pressure by the wing surface area and the angle of attack coefficient. Finally, it finds the takeoff speed by iteratively checking when the lift force exceeds the total vessel weight, returning the critical speed. Example input: vessel weight five thousand, fluid density one thousand, area two, coefficient zero point eight, resulting in output takeoff speed fifteen.

title: Glass Fusing Schedule
spec: A glass artist needs a firing schedule to safely melt and cool a thick glass sculpture. The logic inside `fuse(glass, kiln)` first determines the heating ramp rate and top temperature based on the glass coefficient of expansion and the piece thickness. Next, it calculates the annealing soak time required to relieve internal stress once the kiln cools to the strain point. Finally, it generates the full schedule duration by summing the heating, holding, and controlled cooling phases. Example input: expansion ninety, thickness twelve, kiln power high, resulting in output total duration fourteen point five hours.

title: Macrame Cord Length
spec: A craft designer calculates how much cotton cord to cut for a wall hanging pattern. The logic inside `cut(pattern, cord)` first computes the length consumed by the knots by multiplying the number of square knots and half hitches by the cord diameter and a knotting multiplier. Next, it adds the unknotted drop length and the final fringe allowance to get the total finished strand length. Finally, because the cord is folded in half over the dowel, it doubles the length and returns the initial cutting measurement. Example input: fifty square knots, cord diameter four, multiplier three, drop twenty, fringe ten, resulting in output cutting length two hundred sixty.

title: Falconry Raptor Weight Management
spec: A falconer calculates the daily food ration to keep a hunting bird at its ideal flying weight. The logic inside `manage(bird, conditions)` first determines the metabolic burn rate based on the bird species base metabolism, the current ambient temperature, and the wind chill factor. Next, it calculates the caloric deficit or surplus by comparing the bird morning weight to its target hunting weight. Finally, it converts the required caloric adjustment into grams of quail meat to feed the bird that evening. Example input: species hawk, temp five, wind ten, morning weight nine hundred, target eight hundred eighty, resulting in output ration forty five.

title: Bobsled Track Banking
spec: A winter sports engineer designs the banking angle of an ice track curve to prevent crashes. The logic inside `bank(sled, curve)` first calculates the centrifugal force exerted on the sled using its entry velocity, the sled mass, and the curve radius. Next, it determines the minimum banking angle required to counteract this force while accounting for the friction coefficient of the ice. Finally, it returns the optimal angle in degrees and the maximum safe exit velocity. Example input: velocity thirty, mass two hundred, radius fifty, friction zero point zero five, resulting in output angle sixty, exit velocity twenty eight.

title: Bookbinding Signature Collation
spec: Given a total number of manuscript pages, calculate how to group them into folded sections for sewing. The entry function is `collate(pages)`. Each section contains exactly four stacked sheets folded in half, creating sixteen pages. If the total pages do not perfectly divide by sixteen, add blank pages to the final section. Return a list of tuples, where each tuple represents one folded section containing a sequence of page numbers. The logic must separate the steps of padding the total count to a multiple of sixteen, splitting the padded sequence into chunks of sixteen, and ordering the outer and inner folios within a chunk to simulate how they are printed before folding. For example, given thirty two pages, it returns two sections, each with a specifically interleaved sixteen number sequence.

title: Abacus Arithmetic Bead Simulator
spec: Compute the final numerical value on a traditional abacus after a sequence of bead movements. The entry function is `calculate(moves)`. The abacus has columns representing powers of ten, with upper beads worth five and lower beads worth one. The input is a list of instructions, where each instruction is a tuple containing the column index, a boolean for whether to move a bead up or down, and a boolean for whether it is an upper or lower bead. The logic must divide the process into interpreting a single instruction, applying the mathematical change to a specific column state, and summing the final column positions into a single total integer. For example, moving one lower bead up in column zero and one upper bead down in column one results in a final output of fifty one.

title: Water Slide Velocity Simulator
spec: Predict the final speed of a rider at the bottom of a water attraction. The entry function is `simulate(segments)`. The input is a sequence of track segments, each providing a drop height in meters and a friction category as a single word like high or low. The starting speed is zero. The logic must separate the calculations into computing the velocity gained from standard gravity on a drop, applying friction loss based on the category string, and tracking the total accumulated speed. High friction removes twenty percent of the current speed, while low friction removes five percent. Return the final speed rounded to two decimal places and a count of how many individual segments ended with a speed exceeding ten meters per second.

title: Juggling Pattern Validator
spec: Check if a sequence of numerical juggling throws is a valid continuous pattern. The entry function is `validate(throws)`. The input is a list of integers representing the height and duration of consecutive throws. The logic should first determine the average of the sequence to find the number of objects required. If the average is not a whole number, the pattern is invalid. Next, it must simulate the landing times in a separate step by adding each index to its throw value and taking the remainder when divided by the sequence length. Finally, check for any duplicate landing times, which indicate a mid air collision. Return a boolean indicating if it is valid, along with the integer number of objects used.

title: Semaphore Flag Translation
spec: Convert visual flag positions into a readable message. The entry function is `translate(signals)`. The input is a list of coordinate pairs, where each pair gives the angle in degrees of the left and right arms respectively. The translation process must involve snapping raw angles to the nearest forty five degree increment, converting a single pair of snapped angles to an alphabetical character using a standard nautical orientation, and handling a persistent shift between letters and digits triggered by a specific number sign angle pair. Return the fully decoded text sentence as a single continuous string. For example, an input of two specific angle pairs might translate to a simple two letter word.

title: Labyrinth Key Pathfinding
spec: Determine if a traveler can reach the exit of a maze with one way doors. The entry function is `navigate(rooms)`. The maze is provided as a list of chamber tuples. Each tuple specifies its integer identifier, a required key color to enter, and a list of key colors found inside it. The traveler starts at the first chamber with no keys. Break the traversal down into checking if a chamber can be unlocked with the current inventory, extracting newly found keys from a chamber, and repeatedly sweeping all accessible chambers to find the next available moves until no new progress is made. Return a boolean stating whether the final chamber is unlocked, and a flat sequence of all collected keys.

title: Typography Kerning Calculator
spec: Compute the total pixel width of a word based on individual letter widths and specific adjacent overlapping rules. The entry function is `measure(characters)`. The input is a simple string of text. The process must be divided into fetching base letter widths from an internal directory defaulting to ten pixels for unknown letters, calculating the kerning adjustment between two adjacent characters based on predefined pairs, and summing the total across the whole text string. For instance, an a followed by a v might reduce the total width by two pixels. Return the final integer pixel width representing the required bounding box for the word.

title: Sundial Shadow Length
spec: Calculate the length of a shadow cast by a vertical pole at different times of the day. The entry function is `project(hours)`. The input is a list of hours offset from solar noon, which can be negative for morning and positive for afternoon. The pole has a fixed height of ten units. Separate the logic into calculating the solar angle from the horizon for a given hour offset, computing the ground shadow length from the sun angle using basic trigonometry, and safely handling nighttime hours. Assume the sun moves fifteen degrees per hour and peaks at sixty degrees at exactly noon. Return a list of shadow lengths rounded to one decimal place, using zero for any time the sun is below the horizon.

title: Tapestry Loom Heddle Pattern
spec: Generate the lifting sequence for threads on a weaving loom to produce a specific pattern. The entry function is `weave(rows)`. The input is a list of rows, where each row is a sequence of boolean values indicating whether the fabric pattern should show the horizontal or vertical thread at that position. The loom operates using four lifting shafts. The algorithm should independently map each vertical thread index to one of the four shafts in a continuous repeating cycle, calculate the specific shafts that must be lifted for a single horizontal row to expose the correct vertical threads, and process all rows in sequence. Return a list of tuples, where each tuple contains the integers of the shafts to lift for that row.

title: Kite Aerodynamic Lift
spec: Assess different kite designs to find the one with the highest lifting potential. The entry function is `evaluate(designs)`. The input is a sequence of design records, each providing a surface area in square meters, an attack angle in degrees, and an average wind speed rating. Divide the evaluation into finding a lift coefficient from the angle which is the angle divided by one hundred, calculating the raw lift force for a single design by multiplying the area, the square of the wind speed, and the lift coefficient, and finally filtering the sequence to find the maximum. Discard any designs that generate a lift force below a minimum threshold of fifty. Return the surface area and lift force of the best performing design.
